transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because... I'm having a really hard time at work lately. Every time I have to get near a scaffold, or a roof edge, or, you know, an upper platform now, my head just tells me I’m about to go over. 

It doesn't even make sense to me, because I can see the rails are in place and I know for a fact the setup is safe, but... it just hits me anyway. I feel like I'm going to fall.
Does this intense fear happen only when you are in high places, or do you experience it in other situations as well?

No, it's really just the high places. I haven't noticed it happening anywhere else. 

If I'm down on the ground or just in a regular room, I'm completely fine. It's... it's only when I'm up off the ground, you know, on a ladder or looking over an edge, that it hits me.
How long have you been dealing with this intense fear of heights?
Well, it's been going on for a little over a year now. I'd say about thirteen months ago. We had a stair tower accident on one of the sites, and... yeah, ever since then, I've been dealing with this.
Do you find yourself having unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about that accident?

No, I don't really have anything like that. I don't dream about it, and I don't catch myself replaying it in my head or anything. It's just... when I actually have to go up high, that's when the fear hits. But no flashbacks or nightmares.
